notes.body:
The lower borders (الحدود) are five distinct roles through which divine guidance moves from Allah into the lives of ordinary believers. Imam al-Muizz li-Din Allah names them in his Sunday prayer: the spokesman, the foundation, the culmination, the successor, and the wing — five links in one chain; remove any one, and the chain breaks.

The first is the spokesman (الناطق). He proclaims a new revealed law (شريعة) so all humanity can hear it. In our present prophetic cycle, that is the Prophet Muhammad.

The second is the foundation (الأساس). The foundation guards the hidden, inner meaning — the باطن. **Maulana Ali is the foundation** in our cycle, the legatee who receives from the Prophet what the masses cannot yet receive, holding inner truth steady long after the Prophet's departure.

The third is the culmination — the **Imam of the age**, in whom both outer law and inner meaning come alive together. The Imam sustains and perfects the cycle across time, generation after generation.

The fourth is the successor — the one **designated to carry the mission forward**, bridging the Imam's authority to those below him so that no seeker is ever left without access to guidance.

The fifth is the wing (الجناح). A bird cannot fly on one wing. The wing **extends the reach of the mission** outward in every direction, flanking the central authority so the whole structure never collapses inward on itself.

Together, they form one movement of guidance:

- The spokesman voices it.
- The foundation roots it.
- The culmination perfects it.
- The successor transmits it.
- The wing extends it.
notes.anchor: the five — the spokesman, the foundation, the culmination, the succes…
notes.quote: the five — the spokesman, the foundation, the culmination, the successor, and the wing
etymology: الناطق (spokesman): from the root ن-ط-ق, meaning to speak or utter clearly. The root yields نُطق (speech) and منطق (logic — the science of correct speech). الناطق is 'the one who gives utterance.' The spokesman is not merely a herald; he is the living voice through which the divine Word sounds in the world.

الأساس (foundation): from the root أ-س-س, meaning to lay a base or establish from the ground up. The root gives تأسيس (founding) and مؤسسة (institution). الأساس is 'the base upon which everything stands.' The legatee bears this name because he holds the inner structure of the revelation upright, just as a foundation holds a building after the builders have gone.

الجناح (wing): from the root ج-ن-ح, meaning to lean to one side, incline, or extend in flight. The root gives جنوح (inclination) and أجنحة (wings). الجناح is the part that both balances and propels a bird. The supporting figure in the hierarchy extends the mission laterally, leaning outward from the centre to keep the whole structure airborne.

الحدود (borders): from the root ح-د-د, meaning to cut sharply, to define a boundary, to set a precise limit. The root gives حد (a limit; also a legal penalty — a boundary one must not transgress) and تحديد (definition, specification). The الحدود of the da'wa are precisely defined thresholds marking where one rank of spiritual authority ends and the next begins.

شريعة (revealed law): from the root ش-ر-ع, meaning to set out toward water, to open a path to a source. The root gives شارع (a road; a legislator) and مشروع (a project — something set on a path). شريعة is the divine 'watering-place,' the law that leads every soul back to its source, just as a path leads travelers to a stream.

notes.body:
The numbers seven and twelve are not decorative — they are **the spine of Ismaili sacred cosmology**. The greeting peace (سلام) divides into seven forms from above and twelve from below, mirroring the structure of creation itself; the prayers of the saints repeat that same pattern when they petition for the hierarchy of the mission.

The seven belongs entirely to **the upper world — the prophetic, the celestial, the divine**. The proclaimers (نطقاء) are the speaking prophets who opened new eras of divine law:

- Adam
- Noah
- Abraham
- Moses
- Jesus
- Muhammad
- the awaited Qa'im

Each brought a new outer law while the inner truth remained unchanged. The culminations (أتمة) are the imams who bring each prophetic cycle to its fullest expression, and the caliphs (خلفاء) are those who hold that authority within each cycle. All three groups of seven occupy the same vertical axis as the seven forms of peace that descended from Allah and His angels.

Twelve belongs to the lower world — the temporal, the cyclical, the earthly. Twelve is the count of months in a year, the count of imams within a cycle, and the count of ways peace (سلام) moves between human beings. Imam al-Muizz (ع) makes this explicit when he prays "upon the seven days and the twelve months" — days are celestial, months are terrestrial. The **twelve successors** map onto the twelve human forms of greeting the way months map onto the turning of earthly time.

The passage is quietly teaching that peace (سلام), one of the names of Allah, carries the entire cosmic order within it. Seven and twelve are **the grammar in which creation was written**, and every believer who says "peace be upon you" is reading a verse from that grammar aloud.
notes.anchor: the seven proclaimers, the seven culminations, the seven caliphs, and…
notes.quote: the seven proclaimers, the seven culminations, the seven caliphs, and the twelve successors
etymology: سلام (peace): from the root س-ل-م, meaning wholeness, safety, and freedom from harm. It yields سلامة (wellbeing), سِلم (peace between parties), and إسلام (surrender). The root binds two ideas: being unharmed and handing yourself over. To greet someone with سلام is to offer your own wholeness as a gift.

نطقاء (proclaimers): from the root ن-ط-ق, to speak or articulate clearly. It yields نطق (speech, utterance) and ناطق (one who speaks). In Ismaili usage, the نطقاء are the prophets who speak a new outer law to the world, as distinct from those who guard its inner meaning in silence.

أتمة (culminations): from the root ت-م-م, to complete or bring to fullness. It yields تمام (completion) and تمّ (it was finished). The word أتم means more complete, more whole. The أتمة are those who bring a prophetic cycle to its fullest expression before the next proclaimer appears.

خلفاء (caliphs/successors): from the root خ-ل-ف, to come after, to follow, or to step into another's place. It yields خلافة (succession) and استخلف (to appoint a successor). A خليفة is literally the one who stands where another stood — not filling a vacancy but carrying forward everything entrusted to it.
